title: A feed that shows what else the people who liked your last like have liked, named "What else is like this?"
summary: On Sun 15 Nov at 23:00Z @spacecowboy17.bsky.social (5,812 followers) posted a new custom feed: "You like a post and wonder: what else do the people who liked it like? / This feed helps answer that question. It takes the last post you liked, finds people who also liked it, and shows what else they've liked." The feed's name, shown in the post's embed, is "What else is like this?". The post has 220 likes, 36 reposts and 12 quotes. One minute later a reply tagged @norvid-studies.bsky.social with the words "what else is like this". The maker explained it is "a feed version of what I built as a standalone page 7 months ago". When a user reported errors in another client, the maker replied "Hm, I may have overdone it with blocking bots. Looking..." and 23 minutes later "Indeed. Fixed it now." A confused user was served one of their own posts; the maker explained that the system "treats posts as auto-liked by the author". One user wrote "That's pretty dope! / And after having used it, also very disillusioning. 😄". Quote posts included a one-word "claim" (79 likes), "Oh my god they actually made it", and "Switching to this as my primary feed" (57 likes). In the thread someone proposed a "claims" bot and the maker replied "One cannot gate-keep a simcluster."

made.what: a custom feed, "What else is like this?", built from your most recent like

couldBeShown: One liked post; the other people who liked it; what else each of them liked, as a feed. A user being shown their own post because the system counts authors as liking their own posts. There is no image in the thread apart from one undescribed reply.
